ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI is at the center of some of the highest-impact multimodal work in AI. ChatGPT serves a massive global audience, and enables diverse interactions via text, speech, and visuals. As interactive surfaces grow, models also need to adapt to emerging harm, understand user intent and situational context, and respond appropriately.

The Chat and Multimodal Safety team is responsible for ensuring that OpenAI’s increasingly multimodal models and products behave safely across these experiences. We develop the research, training methods, and evaluations needed to make these experiences safe. Our work sits at the frontier of responsibly deploying powerful AI, in close partnership with Personal AGI, io, model training, and product teams.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Researcher on the Chat and Multimodal Safety team, you will help shape how frontier models perceive and reason the world, and translate that understanding into safe behavior.

We’re looking for people who combine deep technical expertise with strong safety judgment. Strong candidates often bridge perception and language: they may have built vision-language models, worked on modality fusion or image encoders, developed multimodal post-training or evaluations, or advanced safety for image, video, or audio systems.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

- Define and advance multimodal safety research for text, vision, and audio, connecting perception and semantic understanding to safe model behavior.

- Build training and evaluation methods for VLMs, including post-training, safety evals, and interventions that help models respond safely and appropriately in varied contexts.

- Collaborate closely with Personal AGI, Consumer Devices, and product/model teams to translate research into safer ambient, embedded, and personalized multimodal experiences.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have a track record of building or advancing multimodal models, with depth in vision-language models, video understanding, image generation, audio, or multimodal reasoning—and fluency across both perception and language.

- Understand how multimodal systems work end to end, from encoders, projection layers, and modality fusion to cross-modal reasoning, scaling, and inference tradeoffs.

- Have improved frontier model behavior through post-training, using approaches such as SFT, RL, data curation, synthetic data, evaluation, and rigorous error analysis.

- Bring strong research and engineering judgment to open-ended safety problems: you can form testable hypotheses, design decisive experiments and evaluations, diagnose model failures, and translate findings into robust improvements.

Serve as a hands-on support role within the Coffee Product Development team, helping bring new coffee products to life through product testing, sample preparation, and sensory evaluations. 我们以玩家体验为核心，致力于用创新技术为全球玩家带来卓越的游戏体验。作为 Unpublished R&D Product 团队的一员，你将与客户端、引擎、美术、设计及跨职能团队紧密合作，围绕 UE5 前沿能力开展研究与工程化实践，持续完善高品质、稳定高效的视觉设计流程。

我们正在寻找能够"构建设计体验，而不仅是绘制场景"的设计师。

作为一名优秀的场景设计师，你将从空间体验与视觉表达出发，定义环境设计的视觉语言，与美术、设计、叙事及技术团队紧密合作，打造兼具沉浸感、可读性与制作可行性的高品质环境内容。

我们希望你不仅具备出色的视觉表达能力，更具备系统化的空间设计思维，能够在艺术表现、设计需求与技术约束之间建立平衡。

You will report into the Creative Director of the team.

Responsibilities

Environment Design

• 负责核心场景内容的概念设计，从草图探索到高完成度场景设定。
• 探索并定义符合设计方向的环境视觉语言，包括地形结构、建筑风格、材质表现、色彩氛围等。
• 构建具有高度辨识度和沉浸感的环境设计，支撑整体体验与视觉表达。

Design Systems & Methodology

• 构建场景设计逻辑，包括空间布局、视觉语言、设计原则及叙事关联。
• 建立并持续完善场景设计规范，包括尺度体系、模块化原则、细节密度及视觉引导等。
• 在设计中平衡视觉表现、空间可读性及长期内容扩展需求。

Spatial Design & Collaboration

• 与跨职能团队紧密合作，确保场景设计满足空间体验及整体设计目标。
• 设计清晰的视觉引导与空间层级，提升整体体验及信息传达效率。
• 在空间规划过程中充分考虑功能分区、视觉可读性及制作可行性。

Cross-functional Collaboration

• 与3D场景美术、技术美术及技术团队密切合作，确保设计方案具备良好的制作可行性及稳定表现。
• 提供清晰、可执行的设计交付，包括结构拆解、模块建议、材质指引等。
• 持续跟进场景从概念到最终实现的整体质量。

Quality

• 参与整体环境视觉风格建设，建立关键区域的视觉质量标准。
• 根据产品需求及目标平台要求，平衡设计复杂度与制作成本。
• 在探索阶段提供多方向设计方案，快速支持设计迭代。

Team Contribution

• 指导团队成员，提升整体设计能力。
• 参与外部合作伙伴的反馈及质量把控。
• 推动设计经验沉淀，建立可复用的设计方法与规范。

Required Qualifications

• 拥有6–10年以上游戏行业经验，至少参与过1–2个完整项目（上线或关键开发阶段）。
• 具备扎实的美术基础，包括透视、构图、色彩、光影及空间表达能力。
• 具备成熟的场景设计方法论，而不仅仅是优秀的画面表现能力。
• 能够独立完成从草图探索、空间设计到精细设定的完整设计流程。
• 熟悉多种风格化场景设计表现方式。
• 理解空间设计及内容制作流程，对视觉表现与空间体验之间的关系有清晰认知。
• 理解3D内容制作流程及实时渲染流程，具备设计可落地意识。
• 熟练使用 Photoshop、Blender 及其他3D辅助设计工具。
• 具备良好的沟通能力，能够推动设计跨团队落地。

Desired Qualifications

• 具有复杂环境内容制作项目经验。
• 熟悉模块化场景设计、内容搭建及资产复用流程。
• 具备3D能力，包括 Blockout、Layout 或基础场景搭建能力。
• 熟悉 Unreal Engine 基础工作流程，包括场景搭建、灯光及材质基础。
• 熟悉程序化工具（如 Houdini、PCG）或具备相关设计思维。
• 熟悉跨文化设计，理解不同文化元素的融合与视觉表达。
• 有外部合作伙伴管理或团队指导经验。

Portfolio Requirements

请提供3–5个代表性场景设计案例，内容包括：

• 草图探索（Ideation）
• 空间方案（Layout / Blockout / Composition）
• 最终设计方案（Final Concept）

作品集应重点展示完整的设计思路与空间设计逻辑，而不仅仅是最终视觉效果（非常重要）。

请展示不同类型的场景设计案例，并附带设计说明，包括设计思路、空间规划及功能考虑。

如有内容制作或3D落地对比案例，也欢迎一并提供。

如有商业项目成果，也欢迎一并提供。

We will be looking at your past studies, experience, and your personal relationship with games. If you embody player empathy and care about players' experiences, this could be your role!

Advanced Process Control Engineer Job Summary The Marathon Los Angeles Refinery is seeking an Advanced Process Control (APC) Engineer who will serve as a technical leader for multivariable predictive control and optimization applications across multiple refining units. This role is accountable for the full APC lifecycle, from opportunity identification and economic justification through design, commissioning, sustainment, and long‑term value realization. The APC Engineer partners closely with Operations, Planning, Economics, and Control Systems teams to ensure control strategies are aligned with refinery business objectives, operational constraints, and safety requirements. The role requires deep process knowledge, strong analytical capability, and the ability to mentor other engineers while driving continuous improvement in APC performance. The available onsite schedules for the position are 9/80, 5/40 or 4/1. Occasionally after-hours calls occur and support of TAR as necessary. Key Responsibilities: Lead the development, commissioning, and long‑term sustainment of multivariable predictive control (MPC/APC) applications to optimize unit performance, stability, and profitability. Own the end‑to‑end APC project lifecycle, including opportunity identification and prioritization, economic benefit estimation, controller design, model development, commissioning, validation, post‑implementation audits, and continuous improvement. Collaborate with Operations, Planning, and Economics to align APC strategies with refinery business objectives, constraints, and LP signals, translating economic intent into control objectives. Apply cost‑benefit analysis (CBA) to prioritize APC work and ensure engineering effort is focused on highest‑value opportunities. Track, report, and communicate APC performance metrics, KPIs, and realized economic benefits, maintaining accountability for sustained results. Conduct advanced process data analysis and dynamic modeling to identify control performance gaps, root causes, and optimization opportunities. Develop and maintain dynamic process models, inferential sensors, and lab‑bias‑corrected estimators to support APC and optimization objectives. Design and maintain cross‑unit and plantwide optimization strategies, including coordination of multiple APC controllers. Provide technical leadership during APC commissioning, unit startups, shutdowns, turnarounds, and system migrations, ensuring APC readiness and robustness. Develop, maintain, and audit APC and control system documentation, including control narratives, design basis documents, MV/CV/DV definitions, system architecture diagrams, and technical reports. Partner with Control Systems, OT, and vendors on APC platform upgrades, migrations, and cybersecurity‑aligned system changes. Mentor and guide APC and Process Control engineers, serving as a technical authority and promoting best practices in controller design, testing, documentation, and sustainment. Provide training and technical guidance to Operations, Engineering, and Technical Services on APC functionality, limitations, and economic intent. Stay current with industry trends and emerging APC and optimization technologies, applying lessons learned to drive continuous improvement and measurable business value. Education, Experience and Skills Minimum Qualifications Must have a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemical Engineering. Must have at least ten (10) total years of Engineering experience within refining, petrochemical, or related industries with at least four (4) years of those years in advanced process control engineering. Proven experience leading APC applications from concept through sustained operation, including economic justification and benefit tracking. Must be able to wear appropriate PPE in the refinery (respirator), be able to physically perform all tasks in the field and take hair drug test and physical. Ability to access areas of the refinery requiring use of stairs and/or ladders to inspect equipment. Must have a valid driver’s license. (MPC determines valid status.) Must be legally authorized to work in the US without the need for future VISA sponsorship. Travel Requirement is 10 %. (Training and Seminars) Ability to work extended hours, on occasion, including nights and weekends in process operations environment and during periods of inclement weather. Ability to maintain on-call status and respond to emergencies as necessary during off-hours. The available onsite schedules for the position are 9/80, 5/40 or 4/1. Occasionally after-hours calls occur and support of TAR as necessary. Preferred Qualifications Ten (10) or more years of experience in Process Control, with demonstrated responsibility for APC design, commissioning, and sustainment is preferred. Fifteen (15) or more total years of experience within Controls, Economic & Planning, or Process Engineering is preferred. Ability to build/develop advanced multi-variable process control models from inception to commissioning is preferred. Ability to manage APC related intermediate tags and troubleshoot communications or APC related tuning within Honeywell: Experion & TPS/TDC is preferred. Relocation may be available. https://mympcbenefits.com/relocating/ This position belongs to a family of jobs with increasing responsibility, competency and skill level. Rockstar Australia are seeking Senior Graphics Programmers. You will be working with a small but experienced team, ideally taking responsibility for one or more specific game technology areas, but also be capable of stepping outside your comfort zone to work in other areas as necessary.

Candidates must have a strong passion for video games and interactive graphics, ideally having demonstrated technical abilities working in the video games industry or a relevant related field. WHAT WE DO

• Build, optimise and modify game rendering systems and their related tools using C++ and a variety of modern APIs.
• Work within large codebases with an eye for potential improvements whilst maintaining original design/aesthetic intents.
• Create tools to facilitate the rendering systems and game performance as well as improve iteration times and increase the productivity of all teams.
• Produce performant, stable and well-documented code which is often complex and intricate, as well as debug, analyse and optimise code created by colleagues.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Produce stable and reliable code.
• Help to guide and support less experienced team members.

• Use strong communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate with Art and Design to create streamlined, flexible graphics or related systems.

REQUIREMENTS

• 2+ years of professional experience in the video games industry coding rendering systems for games in C++.
• Experience with at least one modern graphics API (Vulkan, Metal, D3D12, etc).
• Previously held a graphics-focused role, working specifically on rendering systems and features.
• Experience in identifying bottlenecks and optimising existing rendering systems.

• Strong theoretical knowledge of 3D rendering techniques.

We're hiring a Manager of Data & Analytics to lead the SevenRooms D&A team — a team of four analysts and engineers responsible for the data products, AI systems, and reporting infrastructure that the rest of the business runs on. Our 2026 roadmap spans the full data value chain: GenAI agents that audit Salesforce in real time, churn and ICP models that drive CSM and AE prioritization, the MRR/ARPV reporting layer that finance and leadership run the business on, and the Netsuite integration that will modernize how we report revenue.

jobs.description: Hiring is one of the most consequential decisions a person makes or receives, and the tools that power it are becoming genuinely agentic. We are seeking a UX Designer I to design the experiences behind our high-volume hiring portfolio at this inflection point. Amazon's Talent Solutions Product Design & Research team is looking for a UX Designer I who brings strong craft, curiosity, and an aptitude for team collaboration. You will work across our associate hiring domain, delivering design solutions for hiring workflows for Amazon's fulfillment centers, customer service, and grocery operations. You will partner with product management, engineering, and research to deliver human-centered experiences that simplify hiring at scale. Amazon hires at a scale few companies ever approach: hundreds of thousands of roles a year across fulfillment, corporate, and technical positions worldwide, with application volumes that can reach millions in a single week. The products you will help shape increasingly act on behalf of the people who power that volume: defining recruiter tasks, supporting candidate inquiries, managing hiring appointments and shift changes. Your challenge is translating systems into interactions that feel trustworthy, purposeful, and in control at high-volume scale. Where a recruiter managing hundreds of open roles can understand what the system did, why, and what happens next, and where a candidate applying to an entry-level warehouse role receives the same quality of experience as one interviewing for a senior engineering position. Key job responsibilities ▪ Deliver design solutions for defined hiring workflows, from research synthesis through interactive prototypes, presenting a variety of solutions and clearly representing the benefits and trade-offs of each approach. ▪ Partner with engineering and product management in the execution and delivery of successful products and services, using a customer-focused, iterative design process. Work closely with engineering to effectively incorporate the capabilities and constraints of the technology stack into your solutions. ▪ Design for AI-assisted high-volume hiring surfaces where the stakes of a bad pattern are amplified at scale. In HVH, AI systems screen candidates, manage appointment scheduling, surface availability windows, and flag qualification mismatches, often acting thousands of times a day across millions of applicants. Your job is to make those actions legible: when the system qualifies or disqualifies someone, the candidate needs to understand what happened and what comes next. When a recruiter sees an AI-generated recommendation or risk flag, it needs to be honest about confidence and give them a clear path to act or override. You contribute to the trust layer between a probabilistic system and a person who may be applying to their first job or managing a warehouse of open roles. That means edge cases, low-confidence states, and failure modes are first-class design problems, not afterthoughts. ▪ Determine best UX solutions based on customer feedback and business goals. Synthesize qualitative and quantitative data to inform design decisions at the feature level. ▪ Communicate design rationale, outcomes, and deliverables clearly to partners and stakeholders. Present and critique work in cross-team reviews to improve your own work. ▪ Apply and extend the use of established UX techniques, templates, and assets. Reuse UX artifacts and keep consistency across your projects. A day in the life You start the morning in a design critique. You have been working on the appointment confirmation flow for a candidate applying to a fulfillment center role, and you come with three directions and a clear point of view on which one is right. The feedback is direct. One direction gets cut immediately. Another gets pushed on details that matter: what does the candidate see if the system cannot confirm a shift? What does the error state communicate? You leave with sharper answers than you arrived with and a revised prototype due by end of week. That is a normal Tuesday. By mid-morning you are pairing with your engineering partner on the spec for an AI-driven scheduling recommendation feature. The model surfaces a suggested appointment window with a confidence signal, and you are working through what happens when availability data is stale or incomplete. You care about that case because your candidate is a first-time applicant who may not know to try again. Together you land on an interaction that is honest about what the system knows and gives the candidate a clear next step without dead-ending them. In the afternoon you notice that the team's shared component for displaying AI-generated status messages does not account for a partial-match state you just hit in your own flow. You flag it, draft a quick proposal with two options, and share it with the team. It is a small contribution but the kind that compounds: patterns that cover edge cases make everyone's work more consistent. You end the day reviewing research synthesis your research partner shared on candidate drop-off during the scheduling step. Two findings directly affect your current design. Do you combine deep technical proficiency in GenAI — foundation models, Amazon Bedrock, agentic architectures — with the business acumen to land AI transformation programmes tied to real customer outcomes? Do you thrive at the intersection of technology strategy and commercial execution? Join the EMEA Go-to-Market Specialist Team to lead the GenAI transformation agenda across one of AWS's highest-growth and most strategic domains.

The Worldwide Specialist Organization (WWSO) is part of AWS Sales, Marketing, and Global Services (SMGS). We work backwards from our customers' most complex and business-critical problems to build and execute go-to-market plans that turn AWS ideas into multi-billion-dollar businesses. WWSO teams include business development, specialist solutions architecture, and go-to-market.

This is a Principal-level GenAI GTM Specialist role responsible for driving enterprise Generative AI adoption across EMEA. Rather than owning a single service, you will own the cross-cutting GenAI transformation narrative — spanning Amazon Bedrock, agentic architectures, foundation model strategy, and emerging GenAI capabilities — and translate it into use-case-led motions that land measurable business outcomes in customers.

What We're Looking For
- Deep technical proficiency in Generative AI: foundation models, agentic patterns, and the Amazon Bedrock ecosystem.
- Demonstrated ability to land AI/ML transformation programmes in enterprise customers translating technology capability into business outcomes by use case.
- A blend of technical depth and commercial savvy equally comfortable whiteboarding a Think Big architecture and presenting an AI strategy to a C-suite.
- Experience building and executing GTM strategies at scale in a fast-moving technology domain.
Track record of operating as a thought leader and trusted advisor to senior customer stakeholders.
- Ability to thrive in a high-ambiguity, high-velocity environment and shape direction without waiting for permission
- Data-driven approach to prioritization using pipeline data, propensity signals, and market intelligence to focus effort where it matters most
- Experience in enterprise technology sales, solutions architecture, or technical business development with a focus on AI/ML or cloud platforms
- Strong written and verbal communication able to author SLT-level narratives, field-facing plays, and customer-facing positioning with equal fluency

Key job responsibilities
- Own the EMEA GenAI GTM strategy end-to-end driving enterprise adoption of Amazon Bedrock and complementary GenAI services through use case led motion, define the narrative, identify high-impact use-case patterns.
- Land AI transformation in enterprises: develop and execute account-level GenAI strategies for priority industries, mapping business priorities to GenAI use cases, building transformation roadmaps, and guiding customers from proof-of-concept to production at scale.
- Operate at the CxO/VP and practitioner level: engage senior business leaders on AI strategy and value realisation while simultaneously working with developers, ML engineers, and architects on technical solution design and adoption patterns.
- Build and execute scaled GTM programmes : design motions including customer roundtables, GenAI workload assessments, use-case workshops, developer engagement, and regional campaigns that create demand and accelerate adoption.

- Influence Marketing: co-develop thought leadership, digital campaigns, and customer success stories that position AWS as the platform of choice for enterprise GenAI transformation.
- Drive cross-functional alignment across Specialist, Field, Partner, and Marketing teams to ensure consistent messaging and coordinated execution

A day in the life
You will lead the go-to-market strategy for one of the most exciting and high-growth domains in cloud. No two days are the same. You might start your morning on a deep-dive with a Fortune 500 financial services CTO mapping their enterprise-wide GenAI transformation roadmap — identifying the highest-value use cases, from intelligent document processing to autonomous customer service agents. After lunch, you're running a use-case workshop with a major retailer's engineering team, helping them see how Amazon Bedrock can power their next-generation product discovery experience and building the business case to take to their board. Later, you're jumping into a pipeline review with an Area AI/ML sales leader to pressure-test which opportunities are ready to move from pilot to production, before briefing a product team on what EMEA customers need next from Bedrock based on patterns you're seeing across dozens of enterprise engagements.

You'll collaborate daily with account teams, solution architects, partner managers, and AWS service teams — connecting the dots between customer business priorities, GenAI technical capabilities, and market opportunity. Your job is to make the complex simple: translating the art of the possible in Generative AI into concrete, use-case-led transformation programmes that customers can execute and measure. You operate as the connective tissue between what AWS builds and how enterprises adopt it at scale.

About the team
The EMEA WWSO AI/ML Geo Specialist team within AWS's Worldwide Specialist Organization owns and executes go-to-market strategy for the full portfolio of AWS AI/ML services. We serve customers across the complete AI lifecycle while also leading the way to drive net new innovative use cases in this domain. Our customers include some of the most technically sophisticated organizations in the world, and our work directly impacts how AI is built and deployed across EMEA.
You will join a team of passionate builders who combine deep technical curiosity with commercial acumen. We operate with a startup mentality inside one of the world's largest technology companies—moving fast, experimenting boldly, and holding ourselves to the highest standards.

Lead Platform Engineer – Cloud & Developer Platforms

Role Overview

As a Lead Platform Engineer – Cloud & Developer Platforms, you will design, build, and operate Guardian's enterprise cloud application platforms and automation ecosystems. You will own critical components of the Amazon EKS platform lifecycle while also acting as a broad platform generalist, supporting automation, system design, and operational tooling that enable application teams to deploy, operate, and scale production workloads safely and consistently.

This role balances deep Kubernetes platform ownership with versatile engineering skills across scripting, Linux systems, automation, Helm charts, CI/CD, and serverless workflows. The focus is on operational reliability, security-by-default patterns, and disciplined platform lifecycle management that accelerates developer productivity while reducing operational risk.

You Are

• A Lead-level senior individual contributor reporting into platform leadership with strong hands-on expertise in Amazon EKS, combined with broad engineering depth across cloud platforms, automation, and systems troubleshooting.
• A technical authority and escalation point who enforces platform standards across production, non-production, and disaster recovery environments, using automation, guardrails, and repeatable practices.
• Comfortable operating with autonomy and sound judgment under ambiguity, applying operational data, platform maturity signals, and architectural principles to guide decisions.
• A pragmatic "get-things-done" engineer who can move fluently between platform design, scripting, debugging, and incident response.

You Will

• Complement deep EKS ownership with generalist platform responsibilities, including:

• Designing and maintaining automation and scripting solutions
• Debugging Linux-level, container, and networking issues
• Improving system reliability through tooling and standards
• Cluster and environment architecture
• Kubernetes and EKS version upgrades
• Node, AMI, and add-on lifecycle management
• Platform security controls and operational governance

• Design and operate CI/CD and automation pipelines for platform and infrastructure components using:

• Jenkins and Groovy
• GitHub and GitHub Actions
• Terraform
• Python and Shell scripting

• Lead the design and evolution of cloud platforms that support diverse workload patterns, including:

• Web services and APIs
• Long-running and background services
• Containerized workloads on Amazon EKS
• Serverless and event-driven workflows using AWS Lambda and Step Functions

• Embed validation controls, security gates, and safe promotion and rollback mechanisms directly into pipelines and workflows.
• Ensure platforms and workloads meet Guardian's observability standards by integrating with the enterprise observability and monitoring tooling, with telemetry and alerting aligned to workload criticality.
• Integrate approved security scanning tooling into delivery and platform pipelines for dependency and container image scanning.
• Act as a senior escalation point for platform-related production incidents, leading or contributing to root cause analysis and driving durable remediation.
• Partner closely with Application Engineering, Security Engineering, Observability, and Architecture teams to influence workload design, enforce secure-by-default patterns, and align with Guardian standards and future-state architecture.
• Mentor engineers and contribute to raising overall platform engineering, automation, and operational maturity.

Required Qualifications(Must Have)

• 7+ years of experience in platform engineering, cloud engineering, DevOps, SRE, or closely related roles.
• Strong hands-on experience with Kubernetes and Amazon EKS, including real-world production operations and upgrades.
• Broad engineering depth beyond Kubernetes, including:

• Linux systems troubleshooting
• Container runtimes and Docker
• Automation and scripting for operational workflows

• Hands-on experience with AWS Lambda, Step Functions, and serverless execution models.
• Strong proficiency in Infrastructure as Code using Terraform or equivalent tools.
• Experience building and operating CI/CD automation using Jenkins and/or GitHub Actions.
• Strong scripting and automation skills using Python and Shell.
• Solid understanding of how application architecture decisions impact reliability, security, and operations.
• Experience designing and operating platforms consumed by multiple application teams at enterprise scale.
• Proven ability to troubleshoot complex, cross-layer issues spanning:

• Kubernetes platforms
• Linux and containers
• CI/CD and automation tooling
• Security and observability systems

Location

Three days a week at a Guardian location in Holmdel, NJ; or Bethlehem, PA.

$118,980.00 - $195,465.00

jobs.description: Are you excited about improving the advertiser experience on one of the world's largest programmatic advertising platforms? As a Technical Account Manager on the Amazon Demand Side Platform (DSP) team, you will focus on improving how advertisers run Deals by identifying patterns in supply-related issues, decreasing time to resolution, and equipping advertisers and account managers with the knowledge they need to succeed. You will work across Client Account Management, SSP Partnership, and Product and Engineering teams to balance quick fixes with long-term supply improvements. You will surface patterns in support tickets that point to larger opportunities — whether that means strengthening the supply network, improving products, or helping clients and partners get more from the platform. This role calls for strong analytical ability and a solution-oriented mindset, because the team designs solutions to prevent problems proactively rather than simply reacting to ticket volume. You should be familiar with industry trends including supply path optimization and emerging formats such as Audio, Digital Out of Home (DOOH), and live events, and comfortable communicating supply-side capabilities to senior business and technical leaders inside and outside Amazon. Key job responsibilities - Understand advertiser goals, facilitate their usage of Deals on the DSP platform, and proactively identify optimization opportunities by working with Account Teams, Product, Engineering, and SSP partners. - Analyze support ticket patterns and key performance trends across clients, then translate findings into data-driven recommendations that reduce time to resolution and improve the overall advertiser experience. - Investigate and root-cause supply issues in partnership with Solution Architects, Product Managers, and Engineering, ensuring timely resolution while capturing insights that inform longer-term product and process improvements. - Provide training and operational support to internal Client Account teams, advertisers, and SSP or Publisher partners, equipping them with the knowledge to resolve common issues independently. - Contribute to scalable playbooks and best practices that raise troubleshooting quality across the team, and share account management expertise with peers. A day in the life You start by reviewing your troubleshooting ticket queue, root-causing supply issues for your advertisers and prioritizing by business impact. By midday, you are partnering with engineering and product teams on a process improvement that will flag delivery issues before a ticket is even created. In the afternoon, you compile patterns from recent cases into a recommendation for leadership, then update a playbook so the broader team can apply what you learned. As you grow in the role, you spend more time designing high-scale solutions with engineering and partners and less time in the ticket queue. About the team Amazon Ads helps advertisers find and connect with customers through a broad set of digital advertising solutions. Amazon DSP is Amazon's programmatic advertising product for campaigns spanning Video, Audio, and Display across Amazon properties (for example, Amazon.com, Freevee, Twitch, Fire TV, and Amazon Music) and tens of thousands of third-party websites and apps. Our team is focused on improving the advertiser experience on the DSP platform, and we are investing in scalable tools and processes that strengthen our supply network for the long term. If you want to grow into a Solution Architect role and enjoy solving problems that sit at the intersection of advertising, technology, and client partnership, we would love to hear from you.
